newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Losers congratulate Hong Kong's leader-in-waiting.
newsitem.headline: Losers congratulate Hong Kong's leader-in-waiting.

text.p: The two contenders defeated in Wednesday's ballot to select Hong Kong's post-handover leader congratulated the victor, shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa, and promised him their support.

"Congratulations on your success," runner-up Yang Ti Liang, the British colony's former Chief Justice, said in a telephone call to the man who will lead Hong Kong upon the handover to China next year.
"I support you one hundred percent, I trust you one hundred percent. If there is anything that I can help...don't hesitate to ask," said Yang, 67.
Peter Woo, at 50 the youngest of the three contenders for the powerful post, urged the people of Hong Kong to support the chief executive-designate.

"We should congratulate Mr Tung, who will become the first chief executive. I call on the six million people of Hong Kong to support Mr. Tung for the sake of a smooth transition and for stability and prosperity (in Hong Kong)," Woo told reporters.
Hong Kong's new elite, a 400-strong Selection Committee carefully assembled by Beijing, overwhelmingly voted for Tung, 59, whose family maritime empire was bailed out by China a decade ago.
Tung received 320 votes, Yang took 42 and Woo polled 36. Two votes were invalid.
